name: Safe database migrations
needs: change a column without breaking the live app
my migration locked the table for minutes
my agent edited an old migration file
summary: Changing the database schema in small steps that the old and new versions of your code can both live with, checked in CI and run as a release step. Renames and drops happen in two releases: add the new shape, move the code and data, then remove the old shape.
need_when: Your app has real data and you change models after launch.
skip_when: Before launch with throwaway data, where resetting the database is fine.

ways.title: Your framework's migrations, checked in CI
ways.how: Django migrations, Rails migrations, Alembic, Prisma Migrate or Drizzle Kit. CI fails if models changed without a migration (for example makemigrations --check) and runs all migrations on a fresh database.
ways.tradeoff: Standard and enough for most apps. The tools don't stop slow or unsafe operations by themselves.

ways.title: A linter for unsafe migrations
ways.how: strong_migrations (Rails), django-migration-linter, or Squawk for raw Postgres SQL flag table locks, non-concurrent indexes and drops of columns still in use.
ways.tradeoff: Catches the ones that cause outages. Adds a few rules to learn.

ways.title: Expand and contract by hand
ways.how: Release 1 adds the new column and writes to both. A backfill copies old rows. Release 2 reads the new column. Release 3 drops the old one.
ways.tradeoff: No downtime for renames and type changes. Takes several releases.

prompt:
Set up safe migrations for this app and plan the change to [describe schema change].

Requirements:
- CI fails if a model changed without a migration, and runs every migration on an empty database.
- Never edit a migration that has already run in production. Fix forward with a new one.
- Split renames, type changes and drops into expand and contract steps that work with both the old and new code during a deploy.
- Create indexes on large tables without locking writes (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on Postgres).
- Backfill large tables in batches in a background job, not inside the migration.
- Migrations run as one release step before the new code takes traffic, and a backup is taken first.
- Write down for each migration whether it can be reversed.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. CI fails when I change a model and skip the migration.
2. All migrations apply on a fresh database with no errors.
3. During the deploy, the old code keeps working against the new schema.
4. A test copy of production data migrates in a known time without long locks.
5. The plan lists which steps are reversible.
acceptance_checks: CI fails when I change a model and skip the migration.
All migrations apply on a fresh database with no errors.
During the deploy, the old code keeps working against the new schema.
A test copy of production data migrates in a known time without long locks.
The plan lists which steps are reversible.
if_you_skip_it: Deploys that take the app down, locked tables, columns dropped while old code still reads them, and migration histories that differ between machines.
how_derek_runs_it: Custody Journal has a migration check script that fails on conflicting or missing migrations, runs every migration forward on a throwaway SQLite database, runs a full rollback and forward cycle when every step is reversible, and proves that irreversible migrations stop a rollback. Its release runbook never reverses migrations: rolling back code is allowed only after a preflight check proves the previous version runs on the new schema.
